THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: A shortage occurs when quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied; a surplus occurs when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded. A surplus occurs when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded. A shortage occurs when quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so there is a shortage. Shortages push price upward. A price above equilibrium creates a surplus because quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

WORKED EXAMPLE: MEASURING A SHORTAGE

runs.text: The horizontal axis is quantity of gas in thousands of gallons and the vertical axis is price of gas per gallon. D0 slopes downward from price $6 at quantity 0 to quantity 300 thousand at price $0. S0 slopes upward from the origin to price $6 at quantity 300 thousand. The curves intersect at price $3 and quantity 150 thousand. At price $2, quantity demanded is 200 thousand and quantity supplied is 100 thousand. At price $4, quantity demanded is 100 thousand and quantity supplied is 200 thousand.

transcript.sourceText: At a price of $2 per gallon, the graph shows quantity demanded of 200 thousand gallons and quantity supplied of 100 thousand. Because buyers want 100 thousand more gallons than sellers offer, the market has a shortage of 200 - 100 = 100 thousand gallons. Upward pressure on price follows.
